summary: TPO antibodies are made when the immune system targets an enzyme in the thyroid. Their presence explains why a thyroid is failing, rather than measuring how well it is currently working.
what_it_measures: The concentration of autoantibodies against thyroid peroxidase, reported in IU/mL.

interpretations.meaning: Positive TPO antibodies indicate autoimmune thyroid disease. They raise the chance of developing an underactive thyroid over time, but on their own they do not mean treatment is needed now.
typical_next_steps: no treatment if thyroid function is normal

when_to_seek_help: Positive antibodies with normal thyroid function usually mean monitoring rather than treatment. Discuss a monitoring interval with your GP.
approved_by: Demo dataset (illustrative values, not for clinical use)
